properties.title: Structure-aware World Model for Probe Guidance via Large-scale Self-supervised Pre-train

membership.reason: Self-supervised I-JEPA-style 2D/3D pose-conditioned latent pre-training for single-frame echocardiogram probe-guidance regression. No persistent evolving state across a rollout and no evaluated future-state prediction.
membership.counting_boundary: Retain as BP_COMPONENT (WT_ACQUISITION); do not count as verified core world model.

properties.backbone: ViT-Small/16 context & EMA target encoders + 6-layer ViT predictor W_theta (hidden dim 384) + pose encoder P_theta
properties.objective: Smooth L1 latent feature prediction loss (I-JEPA style) with 2D masked blocks and 3D relative pose conditioning a in R^6

properties.flow: 2D TTE image -> ViT-Small/16 + fine-tuned W_theta -> 6-DoF probe pose adjustment MAE
properties.boundary: Single-image pose regression at inference; no closed-loop patient or sonographer study.

properties.purpose: Assist junior ultrasound medical personnel in transthoracic echocardiography standard-view probe guidance.

assertions.rationale: Explicitly states individuals in training (290 scans) and test (74 scans) sets are distinct to avoid information leakage.
ViT-Small/16 context and EMA target encoders.
I-JEPA-style Smooth L1 prediction of target-plane latent patch features from context patches and 3D relative pose.
Uses EMA target encoder following I-JEPA [1] to prevent representation collapse.
Predicts latent target-encoder features only (I-JEPA), not pixel-level image reconstruction.
Single-pair cross-plane prediction during pre-training and single-frame pose regression at downstream inference; no persistent evolving state.
3D relative probe pose change vector a in R^6 (x, y, z, rx, ry, rz) conditions target-plane feature prediction during pre-training.
Transitions are over 6-DoF spatial probe pose pairs (at least 150 frames apart for pose diversity), not temporal patient/disease evolution.
Learned 6-layer ViT predictor W_theta maps context features and pose embedding to target-plane features.
Pre-training predictor W_theta is conditioned on 6-DoF relative pose embedding P.
No pixel/image decoder; pre-training predicts latent features and downstream predicts 6-DoF pose.
Downstream fine-tuned head outputs 6-DoF probe position adjustment.
Assisting junior ultrasound medical personnel in acquiring 10 standard cardiac views.
Data collection approved and supervised by The University Science and Technology Ethics Committee.
Downstream 6-DoF probe-guidance MAE evaluated across 10 standard views on 74 held-out clinical scans (Table 1) and 2D/3D ablations (Fig. 4).
Prediction occurs in ViT latent feature space rather than pixel space.

evidence_fragments.content: Structure-aware World Model for Probe Guidance via Large-scale Self-supervised Pre-train
predicting masked structures on a 2D plane and imagining another plane based on pose transformation in 3D space
there must be an interval of at least 150 frames

The three-dimensional spatial relationship between the source image and the target image is denoted as a ∈ R6, which encapsulates the translation and rotation changes in the x, y, and z directions. This vector a is encoded by Pθ to obtain the pose embedding, denoted as P ∈ R1×C.

we amassed data from 364 routine clinical scans, resulting in a total of 1.36 million image and 3D pose data pairs. The whole data collection process was approved and supervised by The University Science and Technology Ethics Committee. We split the dataset into 290 scans (1.07 million samples) for training and 74 scans (0.29 million samples) for testing. For pre-training, only the training set was utilized. Both the training and test sets were employed for the downstream probe guidance task. It is important to note that the individuals in the training and test sets are different to avoid information leakage

The input for this task is an ultrasound image, and the output is the probe position adjustment needed to achieve a specific standard view. This task aims to assist junior ultrasound medical personnel in scanning, enhancing the success rate and quality of view acquisition. During fine-tuning, our pre-trained world model Wθ was loaded and optimized for 5 epochs with a batch size of 1024 on 8 Nvidia RTX-4090 GPUs. The learning rate was set to 1e-4, using a cosine scheduler with a final learning rate of 1e-6. The optimizer was set to AdamW. Evaluation Metrics. The metric used for probe guidance task is the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) between the predicted and ground truth probe poses.

[paraphrase (visual p.7)] Table 1 reports MAE across 10 views (PLAX, PSAX-AV, PSAX-PV, PSAX-MV, PSAX-PAP, PSAX-APEX, A4C, A5C, A3C, A2C): e.g. PLAX translation x/y/z 8.39/8.02/5.53 mm vs Cardiac Dreamer 8.66/8.14/5.63 mm; rotation rx/ry/rz 6.46/5.34/7.89 deg vs 6.60/5.42/8.23 deg; up to 4.34% improvement (A3C x: 6.90 vs 7.21 mm).

we decoupled the 2D and 3D modeling, either focusing solely on 2D structure or 3D structure modeling. As shown in Fig.4, our method achieves improvements in almost all dimensions, whereas using only 2D or 3D modeling results in poorer performance in rotation dimension.

capability_assessments.rationale: Self-supervised 2D/3D pose-conditioned latent pre-training for single-frame probe-guidance regression; no persistent evolving state or evaluated future-state rollout.

limitations: No uncertainty intervals or statistical significance tests reported for Table 1 MAE values.
No external site validation or prospective clinical/sonographer study.
notes: All 10 physical PDF pages read; Figures 1-4 and Table 1 inspected.

legacy_cells.B: Structure-aware World Model for Probe Guidance via Large-scale Self-supervised Pre-train
legacy_cells.C: Jiang, Haojun, Li, Meng, Sun, Zhenguo, Jia, Ning, Sun, Yu, Luo, Shaqi, et al.
legacy_cells.O: Cardiac anatomy in echocardiography; no specific disease condition is stated for the cohort.
legacy_cells.S: Does 2D–3D structure-aware pretraining improve the predicted probe-position adjustment error for acquiring standard cardiac ultrasound views?
legacy_cells.T: 364 routine clinical scans; 290 scans (1.07 million samples) for training and 74 scans (0.29 million samples) for testing; training and test individuals were different.
legacy_cells.V: Probe-position adjustment needed to achieve a specific standard echocardiographic view.
legacy_cells.AI: Ultrasound image patches; 3D spatial probe-pose data
legacy_cells.AJ: ViT-Small/16 context and target encoders; custom 6-layer vision transformer world-model predictor with hidden dimension 384
legacy_cells.AL: Smooth L1 loss between predicted and target visual features; target encoder updated by EMA.
legacy_cells.AM: Image context features, 3D pose embedding, and 2D positional embeddings are concatenated for target-feature prediction.
legacy_cells.BD: Six-dimensional pose-change vector comprising translation and rotation in x, y, and z; units are not specified.
legacy_cells.BI: Structure-aware 2D–3D joint pre-training framework (no distinct model name stated)
legacy_cells.BN: Explicit 2D patch positional embeddings and a 3D pose embedding encode spatial relationships; target features are predicted from source context under the pose change.
legacy_cells.BS: Predicted visual features for masked target blocks on the target plane, conditioned on source-plane context, 2D positions, and 3D pose change.
legacy_cells.BT: Probe-position adjustment output for reaching a specified standard view.
legacy_cells.BV: Smooth L1 feature-prediction loss for masked target blocks; 2D–3D pose-conditioned target-feature prediction.
legacy_cells.DQ: 364 routine clinical scans; 1.36 million image and 3D-pose data pairs; 290 training scans (1.07 million samples) and 74 test scans (0.29 million samples).
legacy_cells.EC: Probe-guidance pose MAE; authors report consistent improvement or comparable results across ten standard views, with maximum stated improvement of 4.34%.
legacy_cells.EJ: Compared against Cardiac Dreamer; the pre-trained model was better or comparable on probe-guidance MAE across ten standard views, with a reported maximum improvement of 4.34%.
legacy_cells.EK: Ablated joint 2D–3D pretraining against 2D-only and 3D-only pretraining; authors report the joint method performed best, particularly in rotation dimensions.
legacy_cells.EL: Authors report slight weakness versus Cardiac Dreamer in one dimension for the PSAX-MV and PSAX-APEX planes.
legacy_cells.ER: Approved and supervised by The University Science and Technology Ethics Committee.
legacy_cells.FB: Image-patch visual feature embeddings (continuous latent tokens) with 2D positional embeddings and a 6D 3D relative-pose condition; the pretrained features support downstream probe-guidance prediction.
legacy_cells.FL: Image patches are encoded by ViT-Small/16 context and target encoders; a custom 6-layer vision-transformer predictor combines source context, 2D positional embeddings, and a 3D pose-change embedding to predict target-plane latent features. The pretrained model is fine-tuned for a downstream head that outputs probe-position adjustment; no planner is implemented.
legacy_cells.FM: The authors introduce a self-supervised joint 2D–3D structure-aware pretraining method that predicts masked structures and target-plane features under 3D pose transformations, using a collected large-scale cardiac ultrasound dataset, and evaluate its effect on downstream probe guidance.
legacy_cells.FN: On 74 held-out routine clinical scans (0.29 million samples), pretraining reduced or matched probe-guidance errors across ten standard views; the paper reports a maximum improvement of 4.34%.
legacy_cells.FP: The authors plan to validate the pretrained model on more downstream tasks and in real clinical settings, with the aim of improving medical outcomes or efficiency.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors identify that prior echocardiogram AI focused mainly on 2D image analysis and neglected assistance for acquiring high-quality echocardiograms; they also note limited prior work on AI-assisted acquisition of target planes.
legacy_cells.FR: The evidence supports improved retrospective internal probe-guidance MAE after structure-aware pretraining. It does not demonstrate temporal multi-step rollouts, closed-loop probe control, prospective clinical benefit, or patient outcome improvement; the authors identify real-clinical-setting validation as future work.
